boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Irish Bend record (April 14, 1863) in Operations in West Louisiana [April 1863]. Grover's landing and skirmishes of April 13 and the Bisland lines (LA006) are context. Campaign-wide movements (the Berwick Bay crossing of April 9-11, the pursuit to Opelousas and Alexandria) and multi-day loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 4th Division, XIX Army Corps [US] and five named Confederate units; the live field reads zero. Irwin puts Grover's whole force at about 5,000 of all arms, Birge's brigade at no more than 1,500 with a fighting line of perhaps 1,200, and says Taylor gives his infantry in the charge as less than 1,000; Grover had eighteen guns with four in action and Taylor four. Taylor says his charging force numbered less than 1,000 against four regiments, a battalion of cavalry and a battery, with a larger reserve concealed.
claims.rationale: Figures from a history and an interested report for different parts of the field; Irwin's Confederate figure repeats Taylor. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Union victory and the live result Union Victory. Taylor says his charge drove the enemy back in confusion and held them; Irwin says Taylor extricated himself from the net; NPS says the Confederates retreated and left the field to the Union.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The Confederate escape is described as the object of the action.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads Total unknown (US 353; CS unknown); the live field reads 355 total (US 355; CS 0). Irwin gives Grover's reported loss for April 13, 14 and 17 as 353 and the nominal-list loss for the battle as 6 officers and 43 men killed, 17 officers and 257 men wounded and 30 missing, also 353; the Confederate loss is not reported, but 21 dead and 35 wounded were left on the field.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Grover's 353 spans three days and overlaps LA008's April 17.

open_questions: Grover's No. 24, Dwight's No. 30, Birge's No. 36 and the other Fourth Division reports, the nominal casualty lists, Mouton's No. 40 and Kirby Smith's No. 38 reports remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Richard B. Irwin's History of the Nineteenth Army Corps (Putnam's, 1892), already registered for the Red River pass, is an interested Union history by the corps' later assistant adjutant-general. Its Teche chapters cite Taylor's report and the nominal lists, so it is not independent of them. Taylor's April 23, 1863 report (Official Records Series I, Volume XV, a shared container) is an interested Confederate account; it is placed in the group of his 1864 Red River reports as one author family. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
